cover.title: Todd Hotes × Zach — Land the Phase 1 Plan
cover.subtitle: Opened as an ex-ante receipt before a 10:00 AM call; closed against the Granola transcript. The deal landed — phase-1 chatbot → Sales Manager at $1,500 — short of a dated build session but with scope, price, and next-step ownership agreed. The ex-ante below is preserved verbatim; every update lives in the diff.
cover.meta: ARCS RECEIPT · Jul 20, 2026 · 10:00 AM EDT · PRL Resins · todd-call.arcs.care

receiptLifecycle.hypothesis: This is not an evaluation and not a first pitch — it is a co-design pass on an already-warm, already-price-agreed engagement. Todd wanting to "explain in detail" is a buy signal, not an objection: he is picturing the build and wants to hand over PRL's real context (sales process, SM routing by geography, the Phase 4/5 resin-recommendation vision). The binding constraint on "landing the plan" is NOT price or willingness — it is alignment on scope + Todd's split attention (fleet/NTSB, the standing Laz opportunity). So "land the plan" should resolve to a concrete first working session / start date, not a signature.
receiptLifecycle.statedPreference: Land the Phase 1 plan on todd-call.arcs.care: converge on scope and walk away with a calendared first working session or an agreed start date — not "sounds good."
agenda: Walk the todd-call.arcs.care plan at Todd's pace; let him drive where he has questions.
Draw out his detailed context — sales process, SM routing, the resin-rec vision — and reflect it back as scope.
Surface and answer every open question in the room; don't leave one unresolved.
Confirm the SugarCRM → Sales-Manager routing assumption is real and that the SM has (or will) see the plan.
Convert: name a concrete first session / start date before the call ends.

diff.expecting: Todd opens warm and collaborative — treats this as building together, not judging a vendor.
diff.revealed: Warm and collaborative throughout — but mobile and distracted: he took the call from the car en route to the airport and never looked at the screen. The depth happened by voice, not by walking the site.
diff.beliefUpdate: Confirmed. Add: his engagement is real but his attention is divided — the artifact has to survive being heard, not read.

diff.expecting: His "questions" are how-it-works / scope clarifications, NOT doubts about value or price.
diff.revealed: Confirmed — zero value or price doubt. He'd barely reviewed the site; his input was forward expansion (capture application/resin data), not clarification. Asked the total fresh, accepted $1,500 on the spot ('keep it simple'), even offered a check + 1099.
diff.beliefUpdate: Confirmed, stronger: the proposal was never in question. Note the ex-ante was slightly off — price was re-confirmed live, not pre-agreed — but it cleared instantly.

diff.expecting: He volunteers PRL detail (sales flow, SM-by-geography, Phase 4/5 resin-rec) — a sign he's already picturing the build.
diff.revealed: Strongly confirmed. Volunteered the full picture: product-dev/application-discovery form, CS-as-switchboard, engineers (not budget) as the buyers, 4-hr lead SLA, lost deals, old-school reps, an 18-yr IT generalist, China/Vietnam/Malaysia. Actively co-designed phase 2+ (voice agents, transcription, photo-to-text).
diff.beliefUpdate: Upgraded. Not just picturing phase 1 — he's scoping a multi-phase sales-automation roadmap. The opportunity is larger than the chatbot.

diff.expecting: The real constraint that surfaces is attention / start-timing (fleet, Laz), not budget.
diff.revealed: Confirmed and sharpened. 'Budget really isn't the driver.' The real constraint is the sales REPS' tech-resistance — 55-60-somethings with paper agendas, 'turning a cruise ship.' Todd gated scope himself: 'keep it simple... getting the rest of the team involved is a huge pain in the ass.'
diff.beliefUpdate: Refined: the binding constraint isn't Todd's attention — it's rep adoption. Phase 1 (customer-facing) correctly sidesteps it; phase 2 must be designed around it.

diff.expecting: "Landing the plan" converts to a calendared session or start date — or reveals a missing stakeholder (the Sales Manager) who hasn't seen it yet.
diff.revealed: Both. NOT a calendared build session. DID land as: $1,500 accepted + payment path agreed + sequenced next steps owned by both sides. And the SM surfaced as the gating stakeholder — Todd forwards phase-1 questions to him and sees him Wednesday at the 'Imagine' meeting.
diff.beliefUpdate: Partially falsified: 'dated session = landed' was too strict for this relationship. Real 'landed' signal here = price cleared + next-action ownership + credential handoff in motion. F2 was right — the SM is the real dependency.

receiptLifecycle.closeNote: CLOSED — the deal landed (better than the base scenario, short of a dated build session). Outcome: phase-1 chatbot → Sales Manager confirmed at $1,500, scope held deliberately simple; a larger multi-phase automation roadmap surfaced, but Todd is correctly sequencing 'this first.' Open dependency: the Sales Manager (credentials + phase-1 questions), routed through Todd (sees him Wed). Zach's next actions: (1) send Todd a short SM question list today; (2) send an itemized $1,500 Stripe link — or check + W-9/1099; (3) get the WordPress login + web-dev-company contact for a sandbox/lower environment; (4) coffee this week. Highest-signal update: the adoption constraint is rep tech-resistance, not budget — it reshapes phase 2, not phase 1.

loadBearingQuote.text: Let's start with this chatbot, and just keep it simple, routed to the sales manager — and then take it from there, because again, getting the rest of the team involved in the technology is going to be a huge pain in the ass.
loadBearingQuote.attribution: Todd Hotes · Jul 20, 2026 — committing to phase 1
loadBearingQuote.significance: One line carries the whole call: the commit AND the constraint, in the same breath. He said yes to phase 1 and named exactly why it's scoped to the customer-facing chatbot — the sales reps' tech-resistance is the real adoption risk, so the wedge that avoids them is the right first build. Everything else he floated (voice agents, transcription, translation) is phase 2, gated on that same constraint.

callWalk.label: Open · warm
callWalk.title: Enter as co-builder, not vendor
callWalk.body: Skip the re-pitch. Open on what you're building together and hand him the floor. He asked to explain in detail — let him, early.

callWalk.label: Depth · his context
callWalk.title: Let Todd explain — and convert it to scope
callWalk.body: As he walks the PRL detail (sales process, SM routing, resin-rec vision), reflect each piece back as a scope line on todd-call.arcs.care. His detail IS the spec.

callWalk.label: Resolve · questions
callWalk.title: Clear every open question in the room
callWalk.body: Answer each question fully before moving on. An unresolved question becomes a post-call stall — and a friend won't chase you to reopen it.

callWalk.label: Convert · the ask
callWalk.title: Name a date before you hang up
callWalk.body: The close is not 'yes/no' — it's 'when.' Propose a concrete first working session. A dated session is the only thing that counts as landed.

signalThreads.label: Relationship
signalThreads.title: Warm, live, price-agreed
signalThreads.body: Close friend; effective CMO/CFO/Comptroller with full spend discretion at a $100M family office. The friends-and-family price is already confirmed. No sales pressure is needed or appropriate.

signalThreads.label: Buy signal
signalThreads.title: 'Wants to explain in detail' = engaged, not resistant
signalThreads.body: Requesting depth is someone picturing the build. Treat his detail as the spec hand-off, not as friction to overcome.

signalThreads.label: Constraint
signalThreads.title: Attention, not budget
signalThreads.body: Todd's attention is split — an NTSB fleet matter and a standing Laz opportunity. The risk to 'landing' is timing and follow-through, so the move is to make the next step small, dated, and easy to say yes to.

signalThreads.label: Alignment gap
signalThreads.title: Has the Sales Manager seen it?
signalThreads.body: The chatbot routes to the Sales Manager in SugarCRM. If the SM was never looped in, internal misalignment can stall the build regardless of Todd's authority. Confirm today.

best.title: Dated first session
best.body: Todd's questions resolve as scope clarifications, he hands over PRL context, and you leave with a calendared first working session and confirmed SugarCRM routing.
best.note: This is 'landed.' File the receipt closed with a start date.

base.title: Scope converged, soft next step
base.body: Good depth conversation, scope aligns, but the concrete date slips to 'let me check the week.' Real progress, not yet landed.
base.note: Close the receipt anyway — the belief update is that timing/attention is the true gate, so pre-propose two specific slots by EOD.

worst.title: Deferred on a blocker
worst.body: Either a genuine value/price question surfaces, or the Sales Manager turns out to be an unconsulted stakeholder, and the plan can't land until that's resolved.
worst.note: Highest-signal outcome — the diff reshapes the engagement. Name the blocker explicitly and make resolving it the next step.

riskFlags.label: SM never consulted (F2)
riskFlags.body: The chatbot routes to the Sales Manager. If the SM hasn't seen todd-call.arcs.care, budget authority alone won't move the build. Ask directly whether the SM has seen the plan.

riskFlags.label: Over-explain, under-convert
riskFlags.body: The failure mode of a warm call is a great conversation with no dated next step. Protect the last five minutes for the convert. A dated session is the only proof it landed.

riskFlags.label: Attention / Laz timing
riskFlags.body: Todd's situation could change (Laz). Frame any gentle urgency around building something he's proud of while he's still the one holding the relationship — never as extraction.

riskFlags.label: Nothing to re-sell
riskFlags.body: Price and willingness are already settled. Don't reopen them. The only open variable is 'when we start.'

protocol.label: Run 01
protocol.title: Hand him the floor early
protocol.body: He asked to explain in detail — let him, in the first few minutes. Listen for scope, not for a place to pitch.

protocol.label: Run 02
protocol.title: Reflect detail back as scope
protocol.body: Every piece of PRL context he gives, restate as a line on the plan. Make him watch the plan become his.

protocol.label: Run 03
protocol.title: Ask the SM question
protocol.body: Confirm whether the Sales Manager has seen the routing plan. Do it as a build question, not a gate.

protocol.label: Close
protocol.title: Name a date
protocol.body: Before you hang up, propose a concrete first session. Then open this receipt and fill the diff while it's fresh.
